title: Environments: workspaces or folders
summary: CLI workspaces (one configuration, several states) against a folder per environment (one root module each, calling shared modules), and why most teams choose folders for dev, staging and prod.

steps.title: One config, several states: workspaces
body: A **workspace** is a named state for the same configuration and backend. `terraform.workspace` is its name:
```bash
terraform workspace new staging      # create and switch
terraform workspace select prod      # switch (select -or-create in Terraform 1.4+)
terraform workspace list             # * marks the current one
terraform workspace show
With the local backend the states live in `terraform.tfstate.d/<name>/`; with S3 under `env:/<name>/<key>`. Everything
else is shared: the code, the provider configuration, the backend and its credentials, the module versions.
That is great for **short-lived copies** of the same thing (a test environment per feature branch). It is risky for
dev/staging/prod: one credential reaches all of them, one forgotten `workspace select` applies dev's change to prod,
and prod cannot stay on the old module version while dev tries the new one. (HCP Terraform "workspaces" are a
different, bigger thing: a state plus its variables, permissions and run history.)

steps.title: Two more workspaces
prompt: `~/infra/api` names things after `terraform.workspace` and is applied in `default`. Create workspaces `staging` and
`prod`, apply in each, and look at where each state lives (`ls -R terraform.tfstate.d`). Finish in `prod` and check
its config: `cat out/prod/api.conf`. Leave the `default` workspace untouched.

checks.name: staging and prod exist and are applied
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/api && test -s terraform.tfstate.d/staging/terraform.tfstate && test -s terraform.tfstate.d/prod/terraform.tfstate && grep -q '^replicas=3$' out/prod/api.conf && grep -q '^replicas=1$' out/staging/api.conf
checks.fail: Both `terraform.tfstate.d/staging` and `terraform.tfstate.d/prod` should hold a state, and `out/prod/api.conf` should say `replicas=3`. Create each workspace and apply in it.

checks.name: default still has only its own
checks.fail: The `default` workspace's state (`terraform.tfstate`) should still hold the `default-...` name.

hints: `terraform workspace new staging` creates it and switches to it. Then plan and apply as usual.
`terraform workspace new prod`, plan, apply. `terraform workspace list` marks the current one with `*`.
`terraform workspace new staging && terraform apply -auto-approve && terraform workspace new prod && terraform apply -auto-approve` (in real life: saved plans).
steps.explain: Three states, one config. Notice how little separates them: the prompt shows no workspace, and `terraform apply` in the wrong one is a single forgotten command away. Teams that use workspaces for real environments add a guard (a `precondition` on `terraform.workspace`, or a wrapper script that prints it in red).

steps.title: A folder per environment
body: Most teams lay out real environments as **separate root modules** that call the same shared modules:
```text
infra/
modules/
app/             the reusable parts
network/
envs/
dev/       main.tf  backend.tf  dev.tfvars      module "app" { source = "../../modules/app" ... }
staging/   ...
prod/      main.tf  backend.tf  prod.tfvars     (its own state, its own credentials)
Each environment has its own backend key, its own pipeline identity (prod's role can only touch prod), and can pin a
different module version while a change is tried in dev. Differences between environments are visible in code
review instead of hidden in `terraform.workspace == "prod" ? ... : ...` branches. The price is some repetition in
the small root files, which tools like Terragrunt (or HCP Terraform Stacks) try to remove.

steps.prompt: Workspaces, or a folder per environment?
items: a throwaway copy of the stack for each feature branch
prod must use a different AWS account and role than dev
try module v3 in dev while prod stays on v2
load tests that spin up five identical copies and delete them
auditors must see exactly what differs between staging and prod
steps.explain: Same code, same credentials, short-lived: workspaces. Different accounts, different versions, different reviewers, long-lived: folders (or HCP Terraform workspaces, which do give each one its own variables and permissions).

steps.prompt: A config uses `terraform.workspace` and someone runs `terraform apply` in prod's folder while the `default` workspace is selected. What happens?
options: Terraform uses the `default` state: it plans to create a second copy of everything (named `default-...`)
Terraform refuses: workspaces must be selected explicitly
It applies to prod, because the folder is prod's
steps.explain: The selected workspace is stored in `.terraform/environment` and nothing in the prompt shows it. `TF_WORKSPACE=prod` in CI makes the choice explicit; a `precondition` such as `contains(["dev", "prod"], terraform.workspace)` stops `default` being used by accident.
